# Link

The Link component provides a flexible way to create links and buttons with proper accessibility considerations. It supports both navigation through URLs and programmatic actions using onClick handlers.

## Best practices

Use the Link component appropriately based on its purpose:

-   `href` prop for navigation links.
-   you can add an `onClick` handler to perform some additional action (such as analytics or tracking) on link navigation, however <em>always create a valid link (provide `href`)</em>, this allows users to open links in new tabs, improves compatibility with screen readers and enhances accessibility.<br/><em>If you do not have a meaningful `href`, consider if it is an action and use `Button` component instead.</em> Refer to the <a href="https://github.com/jsx-eslint/eslint-plugin-jsx-a11y/blob/HEAD/docs/rules/anchor-is-valid.md" target="_blank">eslint-plugin-jsx-a11y documentation</a> for more details.

### Example: Navigation Link

```typescript
import { Link } from '@bolteu/kalep-react';

function MyComponent() {
  return (
    <Link href="/path/to/page">
      Go to Page
    </Link>
  );
```

### Example: Link Enhanced with onClick Action

```typescript
import {Link} from "@bolteu/kalep-react";

function MyComponent() {
    const handleClick = () => {
        // Perform some action, e.g. analytics, tracking, etc
    };

    return (
        <Link href="/path/to/page" onClick={handleClick}>
            Perform Action
        </Link>
    );
}
```

### Example: Link + React Router v6

```typescript
import {LinkProps, useHref} from "react-router-dom";
import {Link, LinkProps as KalepLinkProps} from "@bolteu/kalep-react";

type FancyLinkProps = LinkProps & KalepLinkProps;

const FancyLink = ({target, to, ...rest}: FancyLinkProps) => {
    const href = useHref(to);
    const handleClick = React.useCallback(() => {
        // do something, for example track the click event
    }, []);

    return <Link {...rest} href={href} onClick={handleClick} target={target} />;
};
```

And then use it just as you would use the original `<Link>` from React Router:

```typescript
<FancyLink to="/about">About</FancyLink>
```

### Link + React Router v5

In previous React router versions you can pass the `Link` component to
the React Router `<Link>` in its `component` prop like this:

```typescript
import {Link} from "react-router-dom";
import {Link as KalepLink} from "@bolteu/kalep-react";

<Link to="/about" component={KalepLink}>
    About
</Link>;
```
